title.value: Proving Theorems using Incremental Learning and Hindsight Experience Replay
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the paper and throughout the document.
title.quote: Proving Theorems using Incremental Learning and Hindsight Experience Replay

analysis.description: The paper explores a new method for automated theorem proving using machine learning. It introduces a general incremental learning algorithm for domain-specific provers without relying on traditional speed-optimized search or existing proofs. The approach adapts hindsight experience replay to theorem proving to address sparsity in training data and improve proof quality and quantity on the TPTP dataset.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments and provides empirical results by comparing the new approach with state-of-the-art provers and measuring performance on the TPTP dataset.
type.quote: We compare our approach on a subset of TPTP (Sutcliffe, 2017) with the state-of-the-art E prover (Schulz, 2002; Cruanes et al., 2019), which performs very well on this dataset. Our learning prover eventually reaches equal or better performance on 16 domains out of 20.

name.justification: The paper is centered around the field of Automated Theorem Proving, using incremental learning and hindsight experience replay to improve theorem proving processes.
name.quote: Automated theorem proving (ATP) is an important tool both for assisting mathematicians in proving complex theorems as well as for areas such as integrated circuit design, and software and hardware verification (Leroy, 2009; Klein, 2009).

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses using machine learning approaches, specifically incremental learning and hindsight experience replay, to improve theorem proving.
name.quote: In this paper, we propose a general incremental learning algorithm for training domain specific provers for first-order logic without equality, based only on a basic given-clause algorithm, but using a learned clause-scoring function.

name.justification: The field of Automated Theorem Proving is a branch of Computer Science, which focuses on algorithm development and formal logic.
name.quote: Automated theorem proving (ATP) is an important tool both for assisting mathematicians in proving complex theorems as well as for areas such as integrated circuit design, and software and hardware verification.

name.justification: The paper describes the use of a Transformer network for the clause-scoring function, which is integral to the proposed theorem proving approach.
name.quote: We train a transformer network using spectral features in order to provide a useful scoring function for the prover.

is_contributed.justification: The Transformer Network itself is not a novel contribution of this paper, it is an application of existing architecture to the problem domain.
is_contributed.quote: We train a transformer network using spectral features in order to provide a useful scoring function for the prover.

is_executed.justification: The paper implements and executes the Transformer Network as part of the experimental setup.
is_executed.quote: For training, we use 1 CPU for each actor and 1 NVIDIA V100 GPU for each learner.

is_compared.justification: The Transformer network itself is not compared against other models; the focus is on the theorem proving capability via the learning and scoring function it supports.
is_compared.quote: Our comparison with the state-of-the-art heuristic-based prover E demonstrates that our approach achieves comparable performance to E, while our proofs are almost always shorter than those generated by E.
